facts.fact: The club was founded by Brad and May Caldwell of Shelburne, who moved from the Boston area to Shelburne in the 1960s to dairy farm; Brad Caldwell concluded that a golf course would pay better than farming.
The course sits on a ridge above Shelburne village with views of the Green Mountains and, across Lake Champlain, the Adirondacks; redesigned by PB Dye, the new layout opened in May 2020 (par 70).
facts.source: https://kwiniaska.com/ (via the fetch workflow, release data-kwiniaska kwiniaska_home.html); 2021 club handbook https://files.constantcontact.com/62699bd1101/c7628afa-c594-4a3c-8533-243b5d6bc421.pdf

concepts.name: The Ridge Holstein
concepts.rationale: A Holstein's head for the founders' dairy farm and Vermont's dairy country; read at 32 px by its black-and-white patches and pink muzzle.
concepts.symbolism: the Caldwells' dairy farm, and Vermont dairy country around Shelburne
concepts.interpretation: The breed and the yellow ear tag are interpretation: the source says only that the founders came to dairy farm.
concepts.strengths: A subject no other course has; reads at 1x; says Vermont without a maple leaf or a mountain.
concepts.tradeoffs: Nothing about golf or the lake views.

recommendation: Concept 1 (developer's blanket permission, 2026-10-30 overnight brief; pending the developer's look).
